exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS
exploitedBy.relevance: Disabling DNSSEC validation exposes DNS infrastructure to reconnaissance and manipulation, directly enabling adversaries to gather or spoof DNS information.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS Server
exploitedBy.relevance: Without DNSSEC validation, attackers can more easily compromise or impersonate DNS servers to redirect traffic.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS
exploitedBy.relevance: An open recursive resolver can be exploited by adversaries for DNS-based communication and amplification attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS Server
exploitedBy.relevance: Exposed recursive resolvers can be compromised or abused by attackers as part of DNS infrastructure attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Protocol Tunneling
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted upstream forwarding can be exploited for tunneling malicious traffic through DNS without detection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS Calculation
exploitedBy.relevance: DNS cache poisoning directly exploits dynamic DNS resolution mechanisms to redirect traffic to adversary-controlled infrastructure.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Dynamic Resolution
exploitedBy.relevance: Cache poisoning susceptibility enables adversaries to manipulate dynamic DNS resolution to serve malicious responses.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Fast Flux DNS
exploitedBy.relevance: High negative TTL values interact with fast flux techniques by affecting how long false negative responses persist in caches.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
exploitedBy.relevance: Unrestricted zone transfers allow adversaries to enumerate the entire DNS zone, revealing internal network topology and configuration.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Zone transfer data can be exfiltrated using DNS protocols, exposing sensitive infrastructure details to attackers.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS/Passive DNS
exploitedBy.relevance: A resolver running with excessive privileges amplifies the impact of any exploitation, potentially exposing broader DNS data and system access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Reflection Amplification
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of rate limiting directly enables DNS reflection and amplification DDoS attacks using the resolver as an amplifier.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Install Root Certificate
exploitedBy.relevance: Stale DNSSEC trust anchors are analogous to outdated root certificates, allowing adversaries to present fraudulent but accepted cryptographic material.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Stale trust anchors represent outdated cryptographic trust material that adversaries can exploit to bypass DNSSEC validation.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Gather Victim Network Information
exploitedBy.relevance: Permissive ACLs allow unauthorized parties to query the resolver, enabling broad network reconnaissance of the victim environment.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Escape to Host
exploitedBy.relevance: Without chroot or namespace isolation, a compromised DNS resolver process can escape its intended boundary and access the broader host system.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Container Service
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of namespace isolation is analogous to missing container isolation controls, enabling privilege escalation and host escape.
